Vertex Array Object (VAO) Voxel Rendering is a method that converts voxel data into explicit geometric primitives (quads) stored in GPU memory, leveraging OpenGL's VAO and VBO mechanisms for efficient rasterization [S1, S3, unofficial].

The claim states that VAO Voxel Rendering converts voxel data into explicit geometric primitives (quads) stored in GPU memory, leveraging VAO and VBO mechanisms. The evidence in Source [S1] and Source [S3] explicitly describes the 'Vertex Array Objects (VAOs) technique' where a single vertex buffer object (VBO) is created containing all vertices (explicit geometric primitives) for drawing quads using `glDrawArrays(GL_QUADS, ...)`. The evidence confirms the use of VAOs to specify the format of the VBOs and notes that this method involves storing explicit position and color data per vertex, which aligns with the claim's description of converting voxel data into explicit primitives stored in GPU memory.
